source.title: Image Captioning for Effective Use of Language Models in Knowledge-Based Visual Question Answering
source.authors: Ander Salaberria; Gorka Azkune; Oier Lopez de Lacalle; Aitor Soroa Etxabe; Eneko Agirre

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps the sizes of fine-tuned language models and measures downstream VQA scores, a different measure from pretraining loss that bears on downstream predictability with scale.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the OK-VQA score sweep across five T5 sizes. The paper cites Kaplan et al. for scaling laws, but cited results are not recorded as rows. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy or test loss extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes five T5 sizes (60M–11B) on OK-VQA and reports how downstream score changes with parameter count. The authors describe the trend as log-linear in size. This bears on V6 in a new setting: caption-based, knowledge-based VQA. The sweep is incidental to the paper's main aim, and no law is fitted or extrapolated.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say score is logarithmically proportional to model size, following Kaplan et al., with no slowdown yet. Their main conclusion is broader: caption-based text-only LMs beat comparable multimodal models on OK-VQA, and the 11B model matches a GPT-3 ensemble.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes pretrained T5 models of different sizes on OK-VQA and measures downstream VQA score, rather than measuring held-out pretraining loss or testing compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: The number of fine-tuning steps varied by model size and was selected using a validation split; the study also reports changing hardware and hyperparameters to maintain effective batch size across T5 sizes.
record.problems: The relevant size sweep is on one downstream dataset and measures VQA score rather than held-out pretraining loss. Table 2 gives no uncertainty values for the five scores, despite the paper's general statement that results use three runs and report standard deviations. Training-step selection and hardware/hyperparameters vary with model size.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal split between parameters and tokens.
Effect of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form of loss in other modalities or regimes. The downstream score is not a loss law.
Predictability from pretraining loss; any fitted law or out-of-sample prediction; tasks other than OK-VQA.
Dependence of exponents or allocation on setup and fitting choices; bending away from a power law.

record.verdict_notes: Fine-tuning step counts were chosen per model size on a validation split. Learning rate was fixed, and hardware and hyperparameters changed across sizes. The trend is judged by eye from Figure 3, not a fitted curve, and covers a single downstream task. The record wrongly says Table 2 lacks uncertainty; standard deviations are given for all five models.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict loss on much larger runs.
The compute-optimal allocation between parameters and tokens, including how either grows with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the study measures downstream task scores, not the claimed loss law.
The study tests the model-size arm using OK-VQA scores; it does not test predictability from pretraining loss or other downstream tasks.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and whether curves bend away from a single power law.

relationships.condition: Five CBMT5 sizes, 60M–11B, fine-tuned on OK-VQA v1.1, mean of 3 runs
relationships.reason: Score rises monotonically from 29.2 to 47.9 across the sizes, roughly linear in log parameters, and the authors see no slowdown (R1–R5). No law is fitted or extrapolated.
relationships.display_finding: Scores increased monotonically from 29.2 to 47.9, roughly linearly with log parameters and without observed slowdown, although no scaling law was fitted or extrapolated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
